subject: Post-call: security evidence & retention roadmap (SOC2 / audit logs / DPA)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@atlanticbank.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@atlanticbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: security evidence & retention roadmap (SOC2 / audit logs / DPA)

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have clear owners and timelines. I tried to mirror the pain points you called out and the options we discussed.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Auditability: need per-request audit logs (user id, request id, model used, prompt fingerprint, response id) retained for regulatory review.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II attestation + pen-test summary required for vendor approval.
- Data residency/retention: default retention and possibility to export/store logs for 3+ years; DPA redlines for enterprise controls.
- Encryption/key management: ability to use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on Dedicated/Private deployments.

What Redwood can (and will) provide
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where appropriate) and SOC 2 controls map — attached: redwood-soc2-type2-2026.pdf.
- Audit log schema and sample extract (we can produce CSV extracts or S3 exports).
- Pen test summary and remediation timeline (summary level; full pen-test reports handled via NDA if needed).
- DPA redline template to accelerate negotiations for standard terms; we support specific retention clauses per account.

Proposed next steps & owners
1) Redwood: Share SOC 2 PDF + controls map — owner: Marissa (will send by 2027-03-24).
2) Atlantic Bank: Share security requirement spreadsheet and priority items — owner: Elena (already flagged; please send any additional fields).
3) Redwood: Produce a one-page audit-log sample (CSV) showing fields you requested — owner: Karthik — ETA 2027-03-26.
4) Contracts: Share DPA redline template from Redwood to kick off legal review — owner: Soojin — ETA 2027-03-30.
5) Schedule follow-up with security & engineering to walk the audit-log schema and discuss retention/export options — proposed 2027-04-01.

Attachments included here: redwood-soc2-type2-2026.pdf (summary), I also uploaded a control matrix to the shared Drive. If you want the full pen-test report we can provide it under NDA.

Open items we discussed (please confirm):
- Minimum retention you need for system logs (days/years)
- Specific log fields required for your compliance evidence (you mentioned prompt-level hashing and request_id)
- Whether you need continuous log export (S3) or periodic extracts for audits

Happy to hop on a short follow-up call next week — I’ll wait for Elena’s list and then schedule the 30-min technical review with Karthik.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: security evidence & retention roadmap (SOC2 / audit logs / DPA)

Soojin — thanks for the succinct summary. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and one ask:

1) Audit log fields: we need at minimum: timestamp (UTC), request_id, user_id (or proxy id), model_id, prompt_hash, response_id, and a flag if the request included PII. Can you confirm your sample will include those columns?
2) Retention: compliance needs 7 years for certain audit trails; can you outline options for long-term export (S3 archive vs Dedicated persistent retention)?
3) Evidence: we can accept a redacted SOC 2 and a pen-test summary for initial risk assessment; later we may request the full reports under NDA.
4) Contracts: our procurement will want to start with the DPA and the right to requestpenetration test artifacts.

I’m attaching our security requirements sheet (atlantic-sec-reqs.xlsx) — highlights on tab 2 are what we prioritize.

Can you get back to me with the sample schema and a short note on retention/export options by COB Friday? If so, we’ll aim to align internal stakeholders and then set the technical review.

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Vendor Risk, Atlantic Bank
elena.ruiz@atlanticbank.com

Looping in some technical detail below so we can respond to Elena’s questions with concrete options.

Audit log schema (high-level) — we can produce CSV extracts or set up continuous export to your S3 bucket (preferred for 7+ year retention). Fields we can include out-of-the-box:
- utc_ts, request_id, customer_user_id, model, prompt_hash, response_id, token_count, latency_ms, flags_pii

Retention/export options:
- Hosted API: default rolling retention 90 days for audit (we can provide certified extracts for compliance reviews). For longer retention, we offer periodic exports (daily/weekly) to your S3 with lifecycle policies you control.
- Dedicated / Private: persistent retention on your environment; logs kept per your policy (you control bucket and lifecycle).

Encryption & keys:
- We support platform-managed encryption by default. For Dedicated/Private, we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS — HSM-backed options available).

SOC2 & pen test handling:
- Attached is a redacted SOC2 Type II summary (Soojin sent the PDF). We will prepare a short pen-test findings summary; full reports can be shared under NDA.

Next suggested actions (internal owners)
- Marissa: finalize SOC2 summary doc & controls map -> MAR 24 (today).
- Karthik: generate sample audit-log CSV with the requested columns -> MAR 26.
- Soojin: send DPA redline template to Atlantic Bank legal -> MAR 30.

Attachments I’m adding to accelerate legal and engineering reviews: audit-log-schema.csv (sample schema), dpa-redline-template.docx (Redwood initial redlines).

Happy to join the technical review on Apr 1. Karthik — can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
